transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Evan, Marcus, Ben, Lina, Jared, Sophie, Amir
Links: Roadmap deck: https://confluence.redwood/roadmap-q3, Incident notes: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/2026-04-28

00:00 Priya (PM): okay folks thanks for joining, this is the roadmap launch readiness engineering sync for q3, quick goal is to triage the open blockers from the launch checklist and the April outage follow-up, we have about an hour
00:18 Evan (Eng Manager): yep, I'll start with the resource / capacity updates, we had a couple of spikes last week and i want to show the projected Dedicated pool needs, sorry projection numbers are in the deck but quick tl;dr - we need to increase L40 pools by roughly 15% to keep p95 latency under 250ms for the docs workload
00:42 Marcus (Staff Eng): can i jump in - those numbers look right but i think we can squeeze more via kernel selection and quantization tuning, i did a run with the new sparse attention patch but the transcription on the run shows KV cache as "KV cash" in the logs, so I'd like to clean that up before we publish benchmarks
01:05 Ben (SRE): on the incident side, April 28th - the primary root cause was an autoscaler race + degraded NFS mount for model artifacts, the run showed delayed model loads which caused cascading queue growth, i'm adding the exact timeline to the incident page now
01:26 Priya: good, what is the current status of the autoscaler fix? I thought we had a patch in staging?
01:33 Ben: yes, patch is merged, staging looks stable, we still need to add a safety limit in the orchestration layer to prevent the double-scale event, that's on my plate for next week
01:48 Evan: also want to flag the Dedicated vs Hosted fallback policy - product asked for an aggressive fallback to hosted during overload but legal raised the concern about data residency for enterprise customers, we need a policy that is data-aware
02:12 Priya: right, so for private and enterprise we cannot fallback to hosted unless the customer opts into cross-region fallback, we should make that explicit in the runbook and in the console controls
02:35 Marcus: technical note - the fallback path requires model variant compatibility, if we route to a quantized variant we need regression tests, i propose we add a preflight eval that runs a small prompt set when a fallback happens to ensure quality is within delta
02:58 Sophie (Design): one UI question - in the console when fallback happens can we surface the reason and the approximate cost delta? sales needs that for customer conversations
03:12 Priya: yes we should add that, Lina can you own the UI copy and analytics event?
03:18 Lina (Product Ops): happy to, i'll draft copy and the analytics schema, will share by EOD tomorrow
03:24 Amir (QA): about the regression tests, what's the window for false positives? if we run a small prompt set in preflight we need thresholds defined or we'll get noisy alerts
03:41 Marcus: agree, propose thresholds of max 3% semantic delta on eval set and 1% on token-level match for critical prompts, i'll write that down in the perf doc
04:02 Priya: let's go back to the launch checklist, last we had docs, runbooks, perf, legal sign-off, and dry-run. Docs - who is green?
04:15 Evan: eng docs are 90% done, Marcus has the kernel tuning notes, but the deployment playbook needs a final pass to include the fallback and safety limits Ben mentioned
04:30 Marcus: i'll push the kernel tuning PR today, it's small but has some regression notes, the perf spreadsheet will be updated with the new numbers by Thursday
04:43 Ben: runbook edits i can do by Wednesday, i'll also add the NFS mitigation steps and the autoscaler safety limit step
04:55 Priya: legal sign-off - do we have anything outstanding with compliance? we need SOC2 doc updates and KMS/HSM handling for private deployments
05:07 Evan: legal has one question on retention defaults for the hosted API, they want a clear checkbox for customers to opt-in to longer retention, otherwise default is 7 days ephemeral logs
05:24 Priya: ok add that to the checklist and Lina can coordinate with product marketing for copy
05:36 Sophie: one design ask, clarifying the retention options in the console needs better hierarchy so users don't miss it during onboarding
05:49 Priya: noted, Lina will take that. Next, dry-run scheduling - i propose 2026-05-20 for the canary, with a rehearsal on 2026-05-18
06:01 Lina: i'll set up invites, i'll also include the SEs and top SREs and the CSMs
06:10 Marcus: benchmark note - the canary should include a perf workload with both short and long prompt distributions, last time we underweighted long context which hid a regression
06:27 Evan: agree, ops will also run the KV cache warm-up step to simulate a steady state, we should document the warm-up behavior in the checklist (note: logs may say KV cash or KV cache depending on agent)
06:46 Ben: incident review quick recaps - action items include alert tuning for queue length, NFS fallback to local cache, and additional monitoring for artifact load latencies, i've added provisional thresholds on the incident page
07:05 Priya: any blockers for the canary?
07:10 Marcus: dependent on Marcus's kernel PR merge, and Ben completing runbook edits; both are small but critical
07:22 Evan: also need SRE availability for the window, Ben said he will adjust rota, but need confirmation from oncall leads
07:35 Priya: okay let's recap next steps and owners - Marcus benchmarks and perf doc, Ben runbook and runbook edits, Priya publish checklist + legal retention note, Lina coordinate invites and UI copy, schedule dry-run 2026-05-20
07:55 Speaker 1: (mumbled) seems good
08:02 Priya: thanks everyone, we'll meet asynchronously if anything changes, notes will be posted to the confluence page and i'll follow up with the timeline, meeting adjourned
